speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me what exactly happens when you wake up frightened at night? Do you remember having a bad dream, or do you just feel scared without knowing why?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does she recall the content of the frightening dreams the next morning, and has she experienced any recent stress or anxiety during the day? I need to distinguish between nightmares and sleep terrors to determine the correct course of action.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Difficulty sleeping with episodes of waking up frightened. I also have Yelling and crying during sleep episodes, Temporary post-episode tiredness, Recollection of bad dreams, Bedtime procrastination.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that clarification. Since she recalls the bad dreams and can be consoled, this points more toward nightmares rather than sleep terrors. To rule out other causes, does she snore loudly, gasp for air, or have pauses in breathing during her sleep?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Met all developmental milestones with no significant medical history. Social history: Attends school regularly, with usual playing habits and interactions with peers. Lives with both parents.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does she experience any daytime anxiety, school refusal, or exposure to stressful events that might trigger these nightmares? I also need to check for signs of obstructive sleep apnea, so I will listen to her breathing. REQUEST TEST: Polysomnography
